qs_024:n1.prompt:
You are helping me compare corporate card / expense-management providers ({{vendor}}) before I apply for a company card. If you don't already have them, ask me for: my company domain, approximate monthly card spend, team size, and whether we need physical cards, virtual cards, or both.

Please research and compare at least 3-4 leading expense-management platforms that offer corporate cards, evaluating each specifically on these capabilities:
1. Ability to restrict cards by category, merchant, and amount, with automatic decline/lock of out-of-policy spend at point of sale
2. Speed and flexibility of issuing physical and virtual cards to team members, each with individual spend limits
3. Real-time visibility into company spend broken down by team, category, and merchant (not just monthly statements)
4. Ability to create single-vendor virtual cards for SaaS subscriptions/procurement to isolate risk if one vendor is compromised

For each candidate, note: pricing/fees structure, underwriting requirements (e.g., bank connection, revenue/funding thresholds), accounting software sync options, and any notable limitations relevant to a startup our size.

Use public vendor websites, pricing pages, and reputable comparison/review sources — do not fabricate details you can't verify. Do not sign up, enter payment info, or start an application with any provider.

When done, report back a comparison table (candidate name, pros, cons, pricing, fit notes against the 4 capabilities above) and a ranked recommendation of the top 1-2 choices with reasoning tied to our stated spend, team size, and needs. Flag any open questions (e.g., required documents, credit checks) I should resolve before applying. This is a research/preparation step only — do not apply for or commit to any card provider on my behalf.

qs_024:n2.prompt:
You are helping me apply for a corporate credit card through {{vendor}}, an expense-management platform, as part of setting up company spend cards. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any of these details you don't already have: my company's legal name, EIN/tax ID, business address, date of incorporation, business website/domain, estimated monthly spend, and business bank account details (routing and account number) needed to link banking for underwriting. Also ask for the founder/authorized signer's name, email, and any personal details {{vendor}}'s application requires for a personal guarantee or KYC check.

2. Navigate to {{vendor}}'s online application page and fill out the corporate card application form using the information I provide, double-checking each field before submission.

3. Submit the application using your configured credentials if a login is required, or complete the form as a guest application if that's how {{vendor}} operates.

4. Since this is an asynchronous process — {{vendor}} will review and return a decision later (instantly, within hours, or days) — do not assume approval at submission time. After submitting, check the application status page or dashboard, and if possible, poll periodically (e.g., once every few hours or on a schedule I confirm) to check for status updates (approved, pending, needs more info, declined).

5. If {{vendor}} requests additional documents or verification (e.g., proof of incorporation, bank statements), flag this to me immediately rather than uploading anything on my behalf without my confirmation.

When done, report back: the application confirmation (reference number or screenshot equivalent), the current status, any follow-up documents requested, and the expected timeline for a decision. If the form requires me to review and agree to credit terms or a personal guarantee, stop for human sign-off before proceeding further.

qs_024:n3.prompt:
You are helping me connect my new corporate credit card's transaction feed into our accounting books so spend syncs automatically. Before starting, ask me for: (1) which accounting software we use (e.g., QuickBooks Online, Xero, or another ledger), (2) the name of the card issuer and the last four digits of the card, and (3) confirmation that you may use my already-configured credentials to log into both the accounting software and the card issuer's online portal or app.

Once I provide these, please: 1) Log into the accounting software and locate the bank/credit card feed connection settings. 2) Search for and select the card issuer from the software's supported institution list, or if not listed, check whether the card issuer offers a direct export (CSV/OFX/QFX) or a native integration instead. 3) Complete the linking flow using my configured credentials, matching the correct account to the correct card ending in the digits I gave you. 4) Set the transaction sync to pull historical transactions from the card's opening date if the option is available, and confirm ongoing daily/automatic sync is enabled. 5) Create or map the appropriate expense category/chart-of-accounts entry so transactions land in the right ledger account rather than uncategorized. 6) Run a test sync and verify at least 5-10 recent transactions appear correctly in the books with the right amounts and dates.

Done looks like: the card is linked in the accounting software, historical and new transactions are pulling in automatically, and they are mapped to a sensible expense account. Report back with: the accounting software and card issuer connected, sync method used (native feed vs. file import), how many transactions successfully synced, and any transactions that failed to import or need manual categorization.
